channel.title: CARA Development Blog
channel.description: Weekly build logs from CARA — Companion Assistive Robot for the Aged, an MSc Robotics project by Jayashanka Anushan, Middlesex University Dubai.

item.title: Week 16 — Report Submitted, and the GSM Mystery Finally Cracked
item.description: CARA Week 16 — the thesis report is submitted, and the GSM module's long silence is finally root-caused to a real voltage-margin fault, not a dead part.

item.title: Week 15 — First Integrated Tests — Fully Assembled, and the Drive Train Fights Back
item.description: CARA Week 15 — the robot is fully assembled: first integrated tests, encoder speed control, SMS support and tracking latency cut from 710 ms to about 100 ms.

item.title: Week 14 — New Motors Bench-Tested — Real Torque, Working Encoders, Closed-Loop Control
item.description: CARA Week 14 — replacement motors bench-tested, a defective keypad traced, wristband tracking fixed, the CARA Care dashboard verified, and 4WD wiring ready.

item.title: Week 13 — From Finishing Covers to a Shared-Power Fault — Root Cause Found, Fix Underway
item.description: CARA Week 13 — finishing covers designed, a shared-power fault traced to the 5V regulator, a supervisor meeting, and the report reframed as a standalone paper.

item.title: Week 12 — From Report Audit to a Big Engineering Day — LCD Fixed, Obstacle Fusion Built, Pipeline Verified Live
item.description: CARA Week 12 — the robot drives autonomously for the first time, a faulty battery cell is found, person-following comes online and medicine reminders ship.

item.title: Week 11 — Jetson Drives & Displays Its Own IP — Real Firmware, a Live-Caught Safety Bug, and ROS2 Nodes Go Live
item.description: CARA Week 11 — the full autonomous pipeline runs live end to end for the first time, a dark LCD is traced to power, and a stray test sketch is caught in time.

item.title: Week 10 — Remote Control Hardened, and the RFID Mystery from Week 09 Finally Solved
item.description: CARA Week 10 — remote control hardened for always-on operation, a damaged I2C pin fixed with a bit-banged driver, and the RFID module replaced and working.

item.title: Week 09 — Full Integration Test Finds RFID & Motor Issues, Perception Pipeline Scaffolding Begins
item.description: CARA Week 09 — a full-system integration test surfaces an unresponsive RFID reader and underpowered motors, while the ROS2 perception pipeline grows.

item.title: Week 08 — Camera Tower Complete — Full Assembly Testing Next
item.description: CARA Week 08 (in progress) — Camera tower and remaining wire connections completed on the aluminium chassis, ready for a full assembly test.

item.title: Week 07 — GSM Bring-Up Continues, Camera Tower Assembly Begins
item.description: CARA Week 07 — A7670C GSM bring-up continues on the bench. Camera tower assembly starts, with integrated sensor-counting tests running alongside it.

item.title: Week 06 — Jetson Online via SSH, ROS Jazzy Installed & GSM Module A7670C Received
item.description: CARA Week 06 — Jetson brought online over SSH and ROS Jazzy installed. GSM module A7670C (4G/LTE) received and bench testing started.

item.title: Week 05 — Milestone M3 Reached — Hardware Ready, Jetson Nano In Hand and ROS Setup Begins
item.description: CARA Week 05 — Milestone M3 (Hardware Ready): chassis, motors and sensors integrated on the state machine. Jetson in hand and ROS Jazzy setup begins.

item.title: Week 04 — Fall Detection Live on Laptop, Flask UI Built & SIM800L 2G Issue Found
item.description: CARA Week 04 — fall detection at 60.6% confidence, Flask UI tested on mobile, SolidWorks prototype done. SIM800L failed (no 2G in UAE); SIM7600 ordered.

item.title: Week 03 — Hardware Build — From Unit Testing to a Moving Robot
item.description: CARA Week 03 — modules unit tested, replacement motors fitted and the state machine running. A PLA print, then an aluminium chassis, replaced the kit.

item.title: Week 02 — Architecture Done — System, Software & Hardware Designs Finalised
item.description: CARA Week 02 — architecture finalised and the dual-controller split decided. Physical design sketched, DIY kit assembled, and broken gear motors found.

item.title: Week 01 — Project Kick-Off — Requirements, Literature, and the Research Gap
item.description: CARA Week 01 — project kick-off, literature review, requirements definition, and research gap identification for a low-cost elderly-care robot.
